source_caption:
All Dogs Go to Heaven (1989) is a heartfelt animated musical fantasy directed by Don Bluth. Set in 1939 New Orleans, the film follows Charlie B. Barkin, a street-smart German Shepherd mix who is betrayed and killed by his former partner, Carface Carruthers.

After finding a way back to Earth, Charlie is determined to get revenge and reunites with his loyal friend, Itchy Itchiford. But everything changes when he meets Anne-Marie, a kindhearted orphan who has a special ability to communicate with animals.

What starts as a story about revenge slowly becomes something much more meaningful. Through his friendship with Anne-Marie, Charlie begins to understand the value of kindness, loyalty, and love.

The film features memorable voice performances from Burt Reynolds, Dom DeLuise, Loni Anderson, Judith Barsi in her final film role, Melba Moore, Charles Nelson Reilly, and Vic Tayback.

It stars the voices of Loni Anderson, Judith Barsi (in her final film role), Dom DeLuise, Melba Moore, Charles Nelson Reilly, Burt Reynolds, and Vic Tayback. Set in New Orleans in 1939, it tells the story of Charlie B. Barkin, a German Shepherd mix who is murdered by his former friend, Carface Carruthers. Charlie escapes from Heaven to return to Earth, where his best friend, Itchy Itchiford, still lives, to take revenge on Carface. Instead, he befriends a young orphan girl named Anne-Marie.
